title: Minority Carrier Diffusion Length Visualizer
description: Minority holes random-walk into an n-type semiconductor and recombine. A histogram of the walkers is compared with the analytical solution of the minority carrier diffusion equation, and sliders for lifetime and diffusion coefficient show how the diffusion length L = sqrt(D tau) changes. Includes pulse injection and uniform illumination with a recombining surface.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics

educational.topic: Minority carrier diffusion length and surface recombination
learningObjectives: Explain how minority carrier lifetime and diffusivity determine the diffusion length
Calculate the diffusion length for given material parameters
Predict how surface recombination changes the minority carrier profile
prerequisites: Diffusion current and the Einstein relation

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with a random-walk animation, a live histogram, and an analytical overlay
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students calculate the diffusion length or the surface-to-bulk ratio, then compare with the readout and the random-walk histogram
assessmentOpportunities: Calculate the diffusion length before reading it from the panel
Compare the pulse walker count with exp(-t/tau)
Predict the surface-to-bulk density ratio for several surface recombination velocities

simulationModel.modelType: Monte Carlo random walk compared with analytical solutions
equations: D_p d2(dp)/dx2 - dp/tau_p + G = 0, L_p = sqrt(D_p tau_p)
Pulse: dp(x,t) = N/sqrt(pi D_p t) exp(-x^2/(4 D_p t)) exp(-t/tau_p)
Illumination with surface: dp(x) = G tau_p [1 - (S L_p/(D_p + S L_p)) exp(-x/L_p)]
assumptions: One dimension, low-level injection, no electric field
Walkers step sqrt(2 D dt) per time step and recombine with probability dt/tau
limitations: Histogram noise from a finite number of walkers
First-order surface absorption rule; saturates to a fully absorbing surface at large S
Animation time is normalized to the lifetime
